frequency_question: How often do bilateral transboundary water negotiations overcome domestic and institutional structural friction to reach a signed successor agreement within the stipulated window?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water-sharing treaty renewals or renegotiations between sovereign states involving federal-subnational disputes; excludes unilateral actions or non-binding declarations.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Commission renegotiations
Teesta River Water Sharing Agreement (India-Bangladesh draft)

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major regional bilateral water negotiations with subnational friction; believed to represent the complete relevant class of comparable major river treaty negotiations in the region.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical protocols that do not rise to the level of formal treaty renewals.
skeleton: Total successfully concluded transboundary water treaties versus attempted renewals involving subnational vetoes or federal friction in South Asia and similar river basins.
validity_reason: Institutional frameworks and riparian negotiation dynamics change slowly over decades, making historical precedents reliable through the end of the decade.
